Add SE-EDU Java and Git skills for agents
commitResults.messageBody:
AGENTS.md only asked for Javadoc and a detailed commit
message, so later edits could drift from the course
conventions.

Let's,
* add project skills for the Java and Git standards
* require those skills from AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md
* rename noun-like methods and use American spelling
  so the current code matches the Java standard

Merge branch 'branch-A-CodingStandard'
Merge branch 'branch-Level-9'
Add Checkstyle with the AB3 style config
commitResults.messageBody:
The project has no automated style check, so SE-EDU Java standard
violations are easy to miss during edits.

Let's add the AddressBook Level 3 Checkstyle files and the Gradle
plugin, then adjust existing code so checkstyleMain and checkstyleTest
pass.

Constructors move before methods because Checkstyle DeclarationOrder
requires that sequence. Date formatters and test line wraps change
only to satisfy Indentation and SeparatorWrap.

commitResults.messageTitle: Instruct agents to follow Checkstyle as well
commitResults.messageBody:
Agent instructions cover the written SE-EDU Java standard but not
the new Gradle Checkstyle tasks, so generated code can fail the
style check.

Let's require agents to treat the AB3 Checkstyle config as
mandatory and to run checkstyleMain and checkstyleTest after Java
edits.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'A-CheckStyle'
Add a JavaFX GUI while keeping the CLI
commitResults.messageBody:
Ekud is a terminal-only chatbot. Level-10 requires a graphical chat
window, and commands already print through Ui, so the GUI needs a way
to reuse that text without rewriting every command.

Let's,
* add JavaFX dependencies, FXML views, and a Launcher entry point
* record the last Ui message so getResponse can fill dialog bubbles
* keep Ekud.main as the command-line interface

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-Level-10'
Add Java assertions for internal invariants
commitResults.messageBody:
The chatbot reports user mistakes with EkudException, but internal
assumptions (non-null collaborators, parser contracts, task
invariants) are undocumented. If they fail, the result is a vague
NPE instead of a clear programmer error.

A-Assertions requires documenting those assumptions with Java
assert, not JUnit assertions.

Let's,
* add asserts with comments at construction, parse, execute,
  storage, and GUI injection points
* enable assertions in the Gradle test task so they run during
  `gradlew test`

User-facing validation stays as EkudException. The test-task flag
is a single line so it can be reverted without touching
`run { enableAssertions }`.

commitResults.messageTitle: Share add-command execute logic in one place
commitResults.messageBody:
Todo, deadline, and event commands each copy the same four lines:
create the task, add it, save the list, and show a confirmation.

Copy-paste duplication is easy to drift if one add command later
changes how saving or confirmation works.

Let's move that sequence to a default execute method on
TaskCreatingCommand so each add command only describes the task
it builds.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep parse-and-execute at one abstraction level
commitResults.messageBody:
The CLI loop and the GUI getResponse both parse a line and then
call execute, so each method mixes that low-level pair with its
own exit or dialog-style handling.

Mixing those levels makes the shared step harder to see and easy
to update in only one of the two paths.

Let's extract executeInput so run and getResponse stay at the
level of 'handle one command', and the parse-then-execute sequence
lives in one place.

commitResults.messageTitle: Make TaskList iterable to reuse list formatting
commitResults.messageBody:
Ui formats a numbered task list in showTaskList with its own index
loop, while showFound and showTasksOn already share
appendNumberedTasks. Storage.save uses the same index pattern.

Those loops stay in sync only by convention, and callers must know
to use get(i) instead of walking the list.

Let's make TaskList iterable and format any task sequence through
one helper, including the save-file walk.

commitResults.messageTitle: Name reply-bubble styles instead of command-type strings
commitResults.messageBody:
getCommandType returns values such as AddCommand, which look like
class names but are only CSS keys. DialogBox then switches on those
magic strings, so a typo fails silently as an unstyled bubble.

Let's introduce a DialogStyle enum that owns the CSS class names,
and rename the getter so callers ask for a dialog style rather than
a command type.

commitResults.messageTitle: Read command words from CommandType, not literals
commitResults.messageBody:
List, bye, mark, unmark, and delete each repeat their keyword as a
string when building error messages. CommandType already stores
those words as the vocabulary.

Duplicated literals can drift from the real command word, so a
renamed keyword would still print the old name in usage hints.

Let's take the keyword from the matching CommandType constant so
there is a single source of truth.

commitResults.messageTitle: Split event parsing into named validation steps
commitResults.messageBody:
EventCommand.parse locates flags, slices the argument string, and
validates each piece in one method, so the happy path is buried in
error checks. The usage example is also copied in two messages.

Long methods with mixed levels of detail are harder to follow than
a short sequence of named steps.

Let's keep parse as locate flags, extract parts, parse dates, then
construct, and move flag and field checks into helpers.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reuse one date display format in the UI
commitResults.messageBody:
Ui.showTasksOn formats dates with the magic pattern MMM dd yyyy, which
already exists inside TaskDateTime for task display text.

Two copies of the same pattern can drift, so list output and on-date
headings could disagree.

Let's format calendar dates through TaskDateTime so both surfaces share
the same display form.

commitResults.messageTitle: Explain why corrupt save lines are skipped
commitResults.messageBody:
parseLine catches EkudException and returns null with no comment, which
looks like an empty catch that swallows errors.

A skipped line is intentional: one bad row should not discard the rest
of the save file.

Let's document that reason next to the catch so readers do not treat it
as ignored failure.
